nary_nodes.label: Migrant deaths at border
evidence: At least 57 migrants trying to reach the Spanish territory of Ceuta have died after breaching the border from Morocco, as tens of thousands of people entered the enclave in the past 24 hours.
The Spanish government confirmed the raised death toll on Friday evening.
Earlier in the day, Juan Jesus Vivas, the regional president of the North African Spanish enclave, had told reporters that 34 people had perished, without giving details about how they died.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event involving a large-scale movement of people across borders, often with humanitarian or political implications.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event type fits; minting a subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Mass crossing into Ceuta
evidence: He said about 60,000 people had crossed from Morocco into Ceuta by land and sea, many by swimming around a border barrier stretching into the water.
Video footage on Thursday showed hoards of people, mainly Moroccans, walking around the breakwaters onto local roads.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event involving a large-scale movement of people across borders, often with humanitarian or political implications.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event type fits; minting a subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Sanchez visits Ceuta
evidence: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who travelled to Ceuta on Friday, said his government was mobilising all available resources in response to the situation.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event of government action in response to a crisis.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event type fits; minting a subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Repatriation of migrants
evidence: Sanchez called the crossings a “violation” of Spanish territorial sovereignty, saying that authorities were speeding up the repatriation of this week’s arrivals.
Spain’s Ministry of Interior said some 25,000 people were returned from Ceuta to Morocco so far on Friday.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event of government action in response to a crisis.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event type fits; minting a subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Humanitarian crisis in Ceuta
evidence: Rachid Sbihi, who leads a local workers’ association representing Civil Guard officers in Ceuta, called the situation a “serious humanitarian crisis”, saying thousands of migrants, including unaccompanied children, were sleeping on sidewalks, while others roamed the streets aimlessly.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event involving a situation that threatens the health, safety, or well-being of a large group of people.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event type fits; minting a subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Clashes at border
evidence: At the gates into Ceuta, Moroccan authorities had deployed water cannon trucks and pushed people back.
The charred remains of a bus and seven cars could be seen nearby from clashes with the crowds.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event involving physical confrontation or fighting between groups.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event type fits; minting a subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Supreme Court ruling
evidence: Ceuta authorities have linked the surge in attempted crossings to a Spanish Supreme Court ruling earlier this month that barred authorities from immediately returning migrants who arrive by sea without due process.
nary_nodes.type_definition: A judicial decision or ruling in a legal case.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event type fits; minting a subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: EU reaction to crisis
evidence: European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen on Friday described the images from Ceuta as “unacceptable”.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz meanwhile said he welcomed Spain’s intention not to allow undocumented migrants onto the European mainland, adding that his government was in contact with Spain’s.

France is also in touch with Spanish and Moroccan authorities, French President Emmanuel Macron’s entourage said, and Paris stands ready to help out Spain if necessary, including via the European border and coast guards agency, Frontex.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event involving a formal response or action by a government or international body in international relations.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event type fits; minting a subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: France tightens border
evidence: Earlier, French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said France will tighten its borders with Spain after the recent developments.

He had “given instructions to immediately step up controls at the Spanish border” on Thursday night, he said on X, and also announced the activation of the rapid intervention border force “for in-depth inspections”.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event involving measures taken by a government to regulate or restrict movement across a border.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event type fits; minting a subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Italy threatens Schengen suspension
evidence: Premier Giorgia Meloni threatened to suspend Italy’s open-border Schengen agreement with Spain “to defend our borders and ensure the safety of our citizens”, though Italy does not share a border with Spain.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event involving a threat or warning made in a political context.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event type fits; minting a subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Request for emergency declaration
evidence: Juan Jesus Vivas, the head of Ceuta’s regional government, had called for the national government to declare an emergency on grounds of national security, asking for more police and for the army to be deployed on the border “to guarantee the inviolability of the frontier and citizen safety”.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event where a government formally asks for something, such as a declaration or action.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event type fits; minting a subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Rejection of emergency
evidence: Spain’s Interior Ministry rejected calls to declare a national emergency, saying such a measure does not cover migration crises, but promised additional resources.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event of government action in response to a crisis.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event type fits; minting a subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Mafias spread rumours
evidence: Sanchez said on Friday that the influx of migrants was caused by mafias spreading rumours about the court ruling.
“What has emerged from our talks with Moroccan authorities is that trafficking mafias took a self-serving interpretation of a Supreme Court ruling,” he said.
That interpretation “spread like wildfire in recent hours”.

nary_nodes.label: Activists doubt ruling link
evidence: But activists in Morocco expressed doubt that the ruling was behind the surge, arguing most migrants would have been unaware of such legal decisions.

nary_nodes.label: Von der Leyen's statement
evidence: “We cannot allow anyone to come to our [European] Union without abiding by our rules,” she said on social media.
“Dangerous crossings must stop immediately. Smuggling networks must be dismantled. And [migrant] returns must be swift, as our rules allow.”
